F242 / PR #293 — final deployed two-bounce performance note.

Deployed commit0587a41661, reviewed head0a7ff6de7aea496025df7c5a5f3ba4a792448198; static final performance verdict11e09762fb1d9f863e602d83e45f7540bfad468b.

Outcome: the transition bounce still required SIGKILL on old288d0d078f. The second bounce stopped NEW0587a41661 on SIGINT, with NO SIGKILL. This is the requested live-fleet graceful-stop proof, not an idle/fake-server substitute. Prime performed both bounces; performance observed process identity/disappearance and readiness and collected resource windows. Prime reports15 sessions intact, destroy-unattached on, and one control client after each bounce. These final-state observations do not independently trace every teardown operation's order.

UTC transition receipts (prime-reported except explicitly marked observer bounds):

| Event | Bounce1: old→new | Bounce2: new→new |
|---|---|---|
| Old→new PID | 9783→5540 | 5540→22316 |
| Recipe start | 15:01:27.459 | about15:07:43 |
| Build complete | 15:02:47.6 | 15:09:04.273 |
| SIGINT | about15:02:48; not separately printed | about15:09:04.3–.5 |
| SIGKILL | 15:03:18.237 | NONE |
| Old gone, prime's first-seen view | 15:03:18.505 | 15:09:13.382 |
| Old gone, valid performance bracket | none; see first-probe correction below | 15:09:13.245843–13.346425 |
| New kernel start, performance-observed | 15:03:18.572041 | 15:09:13.605372 |
| New ready, prime receipt | 15:03:20.198 | 15:09:15.228 |
| Build duration | about80.1s | about81.3s |
| SIGINT→old gone | about30.5s, prime view | 8.746–9.046s, signal interval plus own bounds |
| SIGINT→new ready | about32.2s | 10.728–10.928s |
| Recipe-start→ready, build INCLUDED | 112.739s | about92.2s |

Do not call recipe runtime or signal-to-ready time measured socket/reconnect downtime: the socket-unavailability onset was not instrumented. Build time is excluded from the signal intervals. The new daemon stopped comfortably inside the30s external grace in this exercised fleet state; its roughly9s stop is not a universal bound for inherited worker/notice/outer-control joins.

Observer precision correction: Bounce1's originally relayed15:03:18.106703/.212040 marks were stamped BEFORE kernel checks. Their105.336ms spacing is NOT a guaranteed physical-death bracket; probe finish was not retained. The first-bounce receipt explicitly preserves that ceiling and uses the prime's independent gone observation. No negative latency relative to SIGKILL is inferred, and no measurement was rerun to fix presentation. Before Bounce2 the observer was corrected: its bracket runs from last-live probe START to first-gone probe FINISH, including syscall/scheduler time. The100.583ms Bounce2 bracket is compatible with the prime's later first-seen-gone view. Both observers used only in-process kernel start/kill(pid,0) checks and100ms async sleeps, no process launch per poll, no signal from performance.

Resource windows, same retained observer in every incarnation:

| PID / commit | Window UTC | CPU interval s | CPU, one-core average | RSS three readings KiB | Recorded spawns / delta | Machine births/s, separate20s sample |
|---|---|---:|---:|---|---|---:|
| 9783 / 288d0d078f | 14:58:50.650540–14:59:50.676726 | 60.026 | 15.260% | 143280 / 143584 / 143728 | 796→796 / Δ0 | 30.622 |
| 5540 / 0587a41661 | 15:06:31.827157–15:07:31.845204 | 60.018 | 14.546% | 137568 / 139424 / 141472 | 537→537 / Δ0 | 31.625 |
| 22316 / 0587a41661 | 15:12:05.259854–15:13:05.282203 | 60.020 | 15.178% | 224832 / 224896 / 224896 | 510→510 / Δ0 | 24.185 |

PID/kernel-start/commit were stable at every point within each window. CPU is cumulative CPU-TIME slope, never snapshot%CPU; all per-operation spawn deltas were zero in all three windows. Cumulative totals are NOT subtracted across old/new processes. New-daemon windows began after at least120s from their respective kernel starts. Startup/reconnect launch bursts precede these windows and are not covered by quiet-window zero deltas.

CPU after the second bounce is near the old baseline, but no causal CPU saving or zero-overhead claim is supported. The final22316 RSS window is substantially higher than both old9783 and first-new5540—even though5540 and22316 run the same commit. That memory difference is recorded, not dismissed; these workload-uncontrolled windows cannot identify its cause or attribute it uniquely to F242. The two recorded bounce builds were outside their measurement windows, not evidence that all other fleet work was absent. No presentation-improving repeat window was taken.

Machine launch measurement preserves the canonical spawn-rate.py two-PID headline method with /usr/bin/true edges. Its argv attribution/busy loop was not invoked because this seat forbids argv inspection; the same privacy-safe method was used in every window. PID reuse/skips, one-wrap convention, the observer's own end edge and unrelated machine work qualify the headline. No seat/parent/global-majority attribution is claimed.

Cost/remaining ceilings: the static O(C) watch/select footprint remains inside existing connection tasks, not a new task per request/stream; shutdown-only timer/notification fanout and remaining-read fallback launches remain as reviewed. External bounce setter and /bin/sleep polling are not counted by daemon spawn counters. The successful bounces do not close canonical F244: it covers BOTH inherited missing-tmux lookup bypass and the unbounded setter wait after SIGKILL, folded into F243 under prime's C34 ruling. Inherited tail EOF exit also is not automatic tail reconnection. No whole-daemon10s or unconditional whole-helper2s guarantee is claimed.

Receipts:
- /tmp/f242-live-comparison.json (all windows, both bounces and provenance)
- /tmp/f242-before-288d0d07-window.json
- /tmp/f242-new-5540-before-bounce2-window.json
- /tmp/f242-after-22316-window.json
- /tmp/f242-bounce1-complete.json
- /tmp/f242-bounce2-complete.json
- /tmp/f242-bounce1-old-gone.json (raw pre-check timestamp ceiling preserved in complete receipt)
- /tmp/f242-bounce2-old-gone.json (corrected syscall-inclusive bracket)

No product edits, builds, tests, deployments or signals by performance. #293 merged; delivered's holding release is respected, not reacquired merely to publish this requested postmerge note. If the writer flags non-holder, that is truthful publication provenance.

magicWand / encoded observation lesson: stamp BOTH start and finish around a process-state probe; emit signal/old-gone/new-ready at their operations, separately from builds. This run corrected its observer and preserved the failed precision claim instead of manufacturing a better-looking receipt. Canonical harness encoding is proposed, not falsely claimed as a product edit.
